source_refs.note: Topic 20.3.1 with Quick Checks 20.4 to 20.6, answered (PDF 65-68); the mechanisms are redrawn. The book says the sigma complex is 'deprotonated by AlCl4-' in bromination; it is [AlBr4]-. The learning outcomes' 'neutronium ion' is the nitronium ion. Answers need review.

blocks.text: Whatever the electrophile, electrophilic aromatic substitution happens in three main steps.

items: Generation of the electrophile: the electrophile, a positive ion or the positive end of a polar molecule, usually cannot simply be added; it is made in the reaction mixture (in situ) from suitable reagents.

Electrophilic attack: pi electrons of the ring attack the electrophile, forming a sigma bond between one ring carbon and the electrophile. This breaks the aromaticity: only four pi electrons remain, and a positive charge is spread over the other five carbons. This intermediate is the sigma complex (arenium ion).
Restoration of aromaticity: a base (counter-ion) removes the H from the sp3 carbon. The C-H bond breaks heterolytically, its electrons go back into the pi system, and the delocalisation is restored.

blocks.alt: Benzene with a curly arrow from its ring to E+, then the sigma complex: a ring whose top carbon carries H and E, with a broken circle and a + inside and a curly arrow from the C-H bond into the ring. A second arrow labelled Rapid step gives the substituted benzene with E, + H+.
blocks.caption: General mechanism of electrophilic substitution (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 65).

blocks.text: Benzene reacts with chlorine or bromine only in the presence of a Lewis acid, such as aluminium chloride (AlCl3), iron(III) chloride (FeCl3) or iron(III) bromide (FeBr3), which coordinates to the halogen and generates a strong electrophile. For bromination: C6H6 + Br2 -> C6H5Br + HBr (anhydrous AlBr3).

blocks.alt: Benzene + Br2, with AlBr3 over the arrow and ANHYDROUS under it, gives bromobenzene + HBr.
blocks.caption: Bromination of benzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 65).

items: Br2 + AlBr3 -> Br+ + [AlBr4]-: the Lewis acid polarises Br2 and forms the electrophile.
Br+ attacks the ring, giving the sigma complex.
[AlBr4]- removes H+ from the sigma complex: bromobenzene, HBr and AlBr3 (the catalyst) are formed.

blocks.alt: Br-Br with delta+ on the left bromine and delta- on the right one; a curly arrow goes from the delta- bromine to AlBr3. The arrow gives Br+ + [AlBr4]-.
blocks.caption: Formation of the electrophile Br+ from Br2 and AlBr3 (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 65).

blocks.alt: Benzene with a green curly arrow from the ring to Br+, giving the sigma complex with Br and H on one carbon and + in the broken ring. [AlBr4]- sends a curly arrow to that H and a curly arrow runs from the C-H bond into the ring. The arrow gives bromobenzene + HBr + AlBr3.
blocks.caption: Attack of Br+ and loss of the proton in the bromination of benzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 65-66).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed scheme marks the partial charges on Br-Br as sigma+ and sigma-; partial charges are delta+ and delta-, as drawn above. The regenerated catalyst printed '[AlBr3)' is AlBr3.
Chlorination is the same, with FeCl3 or AlCl3 as the Lewis acid generating Cl+.
A nitro group is put on benzene with a mixture of concentrated nitric and sulphuric acids: C6H6 + HNO3 -> C6H5NO2 + H2O (conc. H2SO4).

blocks.alt: Benzene + HNO3, with H2SO4 over the arrow, gives nitrobenzene + H2O.
blocks.caption: Nitration of benzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 66).

items: Formation of the electrophile: H2SO4 + HNO3 <=> NO2+ + HSO4- + H2O. The nitronium ion NO2+ is the electrophile.
Attack: a pair of electrons from the ring bonds to NO2+, forming the sigma complex and losing the aromaticity.
The C-H bond of the substituted carbon breaks and its electrons return to the pi system, restoring the ring: nitrobenzene forms.
Regeneration of the catalyst: HSO4- + H+ -> H2SO4.

blocks.alt: Three steps. Formation of Electrophile: H2SO4 + HNO3 in equilibrium with NO2+ + HSO4- + H2O, with NO2+ tagged electrophile. Attack of Electrophile: a curly arrow from the benzene ring to NO2+ gives the sigma complex with H and NO2 on one carbon; a curly arrow from the C-H bond into the ring gives nitrobenzene + H+. Regeneration of the Catalyst: HSO4- + H+ gives H2SO4, tagged catalyst.
blocks.caption: Mechanism of the nitration of benzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 66).

blocks.text: At higher temperatures more than one nitro group can enter the ring; some 1,3-dinitrobenzene forms even at 50 C: C6H5NO2 + HNO3 -> 1,3-C6H4(NO2)2 + H2O.

blocks.alt: Nitrobenzene + HNO3, with 50 degrees C over the arrow, gives 1,3-dinitrobenzene + H2O.
blocks.caption: Formation of 1,3-dinitrobenzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 67).

blocks.text: In Friedel-Crafts alkylation an alkyl group is substituted into the benzene ring; in Friedel-Crafts acylation an acyl group, R-C=O (an alkyl group attached to a carbonyl group), is substituted, in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst.

items: Alkylation: C6H6 + CH3CH2Cl -> C6H5CH2CH3 (ethylbenzene) + HCl (AlCl3 catalyst, heat).
Acylation: C6H6 + CH3CH2COCl -> C6H5COCH2CH3 + HCl (AlCl3 catalyst, heat).

blocks.alt: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation: benzene + CH3CH2Cl, heat over the arrow and AlCl3 catalyst under it, gives ethylbenzene + HCl. Friedel-Crafts Acylation: benzene + CH3CH2COCl, heat and AlCl3 catalyst, gives the ring carrying C(=O)CH2CH3 + HCl.
blocks.caption: Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 67).

items: Alkylation (three steps): the Lewis acid AlCl3 reacts with the alkyl halide to form a carbocation, the electrophile, e.g. (CH3)3C-Cl + AlCl3 -> (CH3)3C+ + [AlCl4]- (a tertiary carbocation); the pi electrons of the ring attack the carbocation, forming an arenium ion; the intermediate loses a proton, restoring the aromaticity, and the proton forms HCl, regenerating AlCl3.

blocks.alt: (CH3)3C-Cl, the Lewis base, with lone pairs on Cl, + AlCl3, the Lewis acid; a curly arrow goes from a Cl lone pair to AlCl3. This gives Cl(+)-AlCl3(-) still bonded to the carbon, with a curly arrow from the C-Cl bond to Cl. The products are the 3 degree carbocation (CH3)3C+, labelled electrophile - E+, and [Cl-AlCl3]-.
blocks.caption: Formation of the carbocation in Friedel-Crafts alkylation (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 67).

blocks.alt: Forming a new carbon-carbon bond: a curly arrow from benzene to the tertiary carbocation (addition of the electrophile) gives a resonance structure of the sigma complex, the ring carbon carrying H and C(CH3)3 and a + in the ring. Loss of a proton, restoring the aromaticity: [Cl-AlCl3]- sends a curly arrow to the H and a curly arrow runs from the C-H bond into the ring; with -AlCl3 under the arrow this gives tert-butylbenzene + HCl.
blocks.caption: Mechanism of Friedel-Crafts alkylation (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 68).

items: Acylation: AlCl3 forms a complex with the acyl halide, which loses a halide ion to give an acylium ion, RCO+; the ring's pi electrons attack the acylium ion; the intermediate is deprotonated, restoring the ring, forming HCl and regenerating AlCl3. The product is an aryl ketone.

blocks.alt: R-C(=O)-Cl, the Lewis base, with lone pairs on Cl, + AlCl3, the Lewis acid, gives the complex R-C(=O)-Cl(+)-AlCl3(-), which gives the acylium ion R-C(+)=O and [Cl-AlCl3]-.
blocks.caption: Formation of the acylium ion in Friedel-Crafts acylation (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 68).

blocks.alt: A curly arrow from benzene to the carbon of R-C(+)=O, whose O carries a lone pair and a curly arrow from the C=O bond to O, gives a resonance structure of the sigma complex with H and C(=O)R on one ring carbon and + in the ring. [Cl-AlCl3]- sends a curly arrow to the H, and a curly arrow runs from the C-H bond into the ring; with -AlCl3 under the arrow this gives the aryl ketone, the ring carrying C(=O)R.
blocks.caption: Mechanism of Friedel-Crafts acylation (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 68).
